client_id.description: The client this grant is for, and what a revocation addresses. The names beside it are for reading; this is for acting.

client_name.description: The client's own declared name, carried so a user recognises what they consented to. **Not trusted**: a self-registered client chooses this string, and one has called itself *"Fleetless Official Helper"*.

app_id.description: The app the grant was given within. A consent recorded against a client alone would be reusable for a different app.

app_name.description: The app's name as it stood on the consent screen.

role_id.description: The role that tokens issued under this grant carry, and therefore the limit of what the client can reach.

role_name.description: The role's name as it stood on the consent screen. A user consented to a sentence, and every noun in it is stored so the list can show the sentence again.

granted_at.description: When consent was given, as an ISO 8601 timestamp.

grants.description: The user's consent grants, **newest first** — this list exists to be revoked from, and the grant somebody came for is almost always the one they just gave. At most `200`; when there are more, `truncated` says so.

truncated.description: `true` means there are more grants than this response shows. A short page is not a promise that the list is exhausted — and on the one list a user comes to **switch something off**, "I cannot see it" and "it does not exist" is the most expensive difference there is.
